The syndrome involves severe memory impairment associated with thiamine deficiency, commonly in severe alcohol use disorder. In Archipelago, Finnegan tells a Travelers' Aid worker that his trouble is 'Korsakofs Psychosis' [A:244].

A:244

Korsakofs PsychosisFinnegan's name for his memory trouble when speaking to the Travelers' Aid woman. He declines a doctor, saying doctors do not understand the condition and ascribe it to drinking; he compares himself with his father's strange behavior [A:244].

A:244

KosGreek island in the Dodecanese. In Anastasia's account of mermaids, its mermaid beaches were already documented by the beginning of Egypt's Eighteenth Dynasty, conventionally dated about 1550-1295 BCE. This documentation belongs to the novel's mermaid lore [D:34-35].

D:34-35

KrakowPolish city associated with Ifreann Noonan Columkill Gregorovitch's birth in 1830, near Krakow or Skawine, in X's account [D:278]. X places St. Elmo's parish near Krakow and says Ifreann claimed lifelong citizenship of the Republic of Krakow after fleeing the region at about fifteen [D:279-280]. The historical Free City existed from 1815 to 1846; X's statement that it existed only in that one year is inaccurate [D:280].

D:278; D:279-280; D:280

KrautEpithet repeatedly applied to Hans. The narrator first calls him merry-looking and powerful [A:5]. Before their drinking contest Bushmaster boasts of having beaten krauts, and during it he calls Hans an American kraut [A:15] [A:22]. Another description makes this 'kraut-head' simultaneously Faust and Apollo [A:169].

A:5; A:15; A:22; A:169

Kreb's Cycle ConsonanceOne of the supposed age-measuring criteria in the fictional Eighteenth Book of Strange Encounters, written by the editors of the Sixteenth and Seventeenth Books. Along with birefringence flow index and Howship's lacunar frequency, it is said to indicate that Duffey is over four thousand years old, despite a body appearing about fifty-five [MTM B8:250].

MTM B8:250

KristineWoman in Johnny Duckwalk's barroom story, set uncertainly in Lisbon or Stockholm. She offers money to have her supposedly insured husband killed with an axe. Duckwalk and his shipmate Mike Merganser discover that each was being set up as the other's victim; Kristine admits she wanted their rolls of money [D:246-247].

D:246-247

Kropotkin, PeterRussian anarchist thinker Peter Kropotkin (1842-1921), author of The Conquest of Bread (1892) and Mutual Aid (1902), who emphasized cooperative social life and opposed state compulsion. X says that Ifreann Gregorovitch became an ironic disciple after his involvement in the Paris Commune; he contrasts the supposedly crooked saint Kropotkin with the honest devil Ifreann [D:280]. This Ifreann is the father of Papadiabolous I, not Papadiabolous I himself [D:285].

D:280; D:285

KrymX's Russian name for Crimea in his account of the Devil's prison. He dates the imprisonment to 946 or 947 and describes a prison dug beneath the Crimean Mountains [MTM B6:204]. Absalom Stein dates the release after a thousand years to 1946 [MTM B6:185].

MTM B6:204; MTM B6:185

KumanekOne of the godfather or sponsor titles used while the narrator questions Duffey's relationship to his talismanic children, especially Casey: Pate, Kumanek, Nonos, Nasho, Athair Baiste, Sponsor, Padrino, Godfather. The passage asks whether his role exceeds ordinary sponsorship and resembles that of a creating sorcerer [MTM B4:119].

MTM B4:119

KuriPlace-name in Finnegan's verse, grouped with Roi, Rangoon, Kandi, and Cai as places where summer is eternal [A:171].

A:171

Kutz (Soft-Talk Susie)Soft-Talk Susie Kutz, barmaid at the Old Wooden Ship and an angel unaware. Her reports to the Lord make the patrons seem a little better than they are and help account for their unexpected prosperity; the narrative distinguishes regulars from the more casual visitors Finnegan and Le Marin [D:216]. Some later accounts of the patrons are said to derive from her blessed reports, whose relation to truth the narrator leaves playfully open [D:225].

D:216; D:225

Kymatic patternsElectrical patterns in the brain, contrasted with akymatic patterns, in Casey Szymansky's discussion of spirits reading brain activity. He distinguishes verbal, subliminal, electrical, and chemical indications from access to the immaterial mind, and says the spirits must use physical means [PG:539-540].

PG:539-540

L'Ouverture, ToussaintHaitian revolutionary leader Toussaint Louverture (c. 1743-1803). Carmody Overlark's fictional Studies in the Imagination includes him in a catalogue of supposed Neanderthal-like 'pumpkin heads,' alongside Plato, Homer, Aquinas, Rabelais, Luther, Christopher Smart, Rasputin, and Steinmetz. Overlark associates this imagined type with criminals, religious innovators, leaders, poets, and inventors [D:270-272].

D:270-272

La BarqueFrench words meaning 'the boat' in the caption to Henry's dream of a storm on a lake. As wind and waves grow more convincing, he recognizes the biblical wording and prefers the Vulgate's Latin to the French [A:45]. The allusion is Luke 8:23, where the sleeping Jesus' boat takes in water during a squall.

A:45

La PazPlace-name in the poem by Finnegan that Dotty discovers: 'I ought to go visit La Paz and Lierre / And make them acquainted with me' [A:173].

A:173

Ladies' BarOne of the Plaza's forty-eight bars; the narrator jokes that the Ladies' Bar has never known man [A:3].

A:3

Lafitte, JeanPirate and privateer Jean Lafitte, probably born in the early 1780s, whose men and supplies helped Andrew Jackson's defense of New Orleans in 1815; the details of his death are uncertain. In Casey's imagined revolutionary uprising, torpedoes carrying sawed-off shotguns take the role of Jean Lafitte's pirates among the rising workers [A:160].

A:160

Lake BorgneLake in the New Orleans region where the House, Home and Happenings article locates Zabotski and Widow Waldo's dwelling on Pristine Cove [MTM B9:267]. Zabotski tells a reporter he plans to move his great structure there and describes the lake as opening into the Gulf [MTM B9:289]. During the flood the contraption reaches Lake Borgne and rides on a small kedge anchor [MTM B9:287]. The later Zabotski Flats comprise two hundred lakeside acres, two-thirds sweet meadow and one-third salt meadow, extraordinarily lush in contrast to neighboring land; Zabotski attributes the improvement to God's favor [MTM B12:362].

MTM B9:267; MTM B9:289; MTM B9:287; MTM B12:362

LambAn emblem on Henry's dream ship Navicula Petri, among the Greek Cross, Fish, and Six-Pointed Star [A:44]. In Christian symbolism the lamb represents Christ, the Lamb of God.

A:44

Land of BehestOne of the Argo's former names. In its narrated history St. Brandon sails it from Ireland to America, encounters the great fish Jascoyne, and carries Judas, who is said not to be its most hellish passenger [MTM B13:404]. Brandon is the voyager St. Brendan of Clonfert, traditionally dated c. 484-577; the American voyage here belongs to the ship's legendary history.

MTM B13:404

Land of the CyclopsTexas in the narrative of Finnegan's bewildered wandering: a dread country of tall, one-eyed or squint-eyed men where he despairs of seeing home and friends again [A:201]. The comparison evokes Odysseus's encounter with the Cyclopes in Book 9 of the Odyssey.

A:201

Land of the Lotus EatersThe Lotus Eaters tavern, where Hans and Marie arrange a date and where he waits for her [A:16] [A:25]. Its clock is painted and its calendar permanently reads the thirty-first of spring. Katie keeps their glasses filled; inside it remains afternoon even when they finally emerge into a late night outside [A:29]. Its name recalls the Odyssey's Lotus-eaters, while 'always afternoon' closely echoes Tennyson's The Lotos-Eaters. Marie jokingly attributes the saying to her uncle Horace Higgenbotham [A:16].

A:16; A:25; A:29

LangenscheidtGerman language-learning publisher founded by Gustav Langenscheidt in Berlin in 1856. Its manuals are among the books Casey uses at Duffey's, alongside Thimms, Hugos, Marlboroughs, Berlitz, Cortina, and the German-written Metoula manuals [A:159].

A:159

LaonomeMary Virginia's ancient name in Teresa Showboat's account of the companions' Argonaut identities: 'Mary Virginia is Laonome' [MTM B7:234]. Mary Virginia recalls fragments of that life and says she hated the name then and still does; her own reply prints the variant 'Laonone' [MTM B7:235].

MTM B7:234; MTM B7:235

Larkin, LoyRed-haired stewardess whom Finnegan and Vincent meet with Margaret in a city lounge; she claims to have a man in every major port [A:2]. The narrator calls her a pink cloud [A:6], and Finnegan addresses his “Antipodal Ode to Loy Larkin,” celebrating her in Sydney Town [A:32]. Her letter to John Solli, headed Cambeltown, New South Wales, Thursday February 11, 1943, invites the friends to meet the train at 7:45 a.m. for a picnic. It includes Hans, Marie, Vincent, and the as-yet-unmet Casey; she and Margaret profess love for the friends, while Loy complains that her November garden is all weeds and says her father killed the fatted calf for her return [A:27]. Much later Finnegan sketches her again as a pink cloud [A:278].

A:2; A:6; A:32; A:27; A:278

LarkinsLoy Larkin's family, named by Marie Monaghan with the Murpheys among the old Irish families in Australia. Marie gives her own Monaghan family a residence of 156 years, then adds that the Larkins and Murpheys are old families too [A:7].

A:7

LarriganOne surname in the worldwide Angelino clan, listed beside Obermeyer, Viskochil, Borg, and Trevino [A:218].

A:218

Last JudgementIn Christian teaching, the final judgment of humanity at Christ's return, distinguished from the particular judgment at death. In 'The Casey Machine,' a soggy sinner asks his pastor whether everyone will know all other people's thoughts and deeds after the General or Particular Judgment. The pastor says this knowledge brings joy to the saved and suffering to the damned; the sinner perversely anticipates enjoying everyone else's shame [CM:504].

CM:504

Last Night of Her Life, The (perfume)Perfume Margaret Stone wears before the visit to the Decatur Street Opera House [MTM B11:346]. Its name anticipates her death there at the hands of the thunder colt [MTM B11:351].

MTM B11:346; MTM B11:351

Last Rally, theThe gathering summoned by bells rung by a few opponents of the destruction of the world's central institution, the Ekklesia. The narrative immediately locates Finnegan's return to the Argo in the Third Year of the Bells [MTM B13:450].

MTM B13:450

Lateral line remainder of the post-auditory placodesAn alleged anatomical age-marker listed in the fictional Eighteenth Book of Strange Encounters among the tests said to show Duffey is over four thousand years old, even though his present body appears about fifty-five [MTM B8:250].

MTM B8:250

LatinLanguage of education, scriptural echoes, and inscriptions throughout the books. Latin is among the subjects at Duffey's boarding school, where Sebastian excels; Charlotte says 'Sum etiam erudita ipse,' glossed as 'I'm educated myself' [MTM B1:25] [MTM B3:80]. Finnegan begins with a Latin creation formula, and Vincent wishes he could render his two-men-in-a-bar beginning in Latin [A:2]. It is Marie who tells Sally that charity is a Latin word for love [A:9]. Henry's Navicula Petri dream carries the mottoes 'Ih hoc signo vincet,' 'Nisi esses sollicitus,' 'Ubicumque fuerit corpus illic congregabuntur et aquilas,' 'Tu es Petrus,' 'Portae inferi non praevalebunt,' and 'tibi dabo claves regni'; the second is crossed out and replaced with 'If you can't be careful, be good' [A:44]. The storm is narrated in Latin before a French caption appears [A:45]. Casey's notebook gives supposed Latin-to-Germanic sound correspondences, including K to H, F to B, and P to F [A:163]. Hans learns Latin from his father John William [A:208]. The noon-day devils address Finnegan with 'Dic ut lapides isti panes fiant' [A:205]. A Latin scroll identifies the risen Count in Finnegan's self-portrait, and the Argo bringing the Peter-Bell displays its name in Latin, Greek, Hebrew, and Chaldee letters [MB:551] [MB:577].

MTM B1:25; MTM B3:80; A:2; A:9; A:44; A:45; A:163; A:208; A:205; MB:551; MB:577

Laughing Prince of TartaryA formidable adversary within the group called Evil Prince, Purple Prince, Mocking Prince, and Laughing Prince; the Laughing Prince of Tartary may be the strongest and trickiest of them. Reportedly the Prince of the Third Way, he claims allegiance to neither God nor the Devil and says both have rejected him [MTM B13:437-438]. Reports connect him with the dialectic pit, concealed partisanship, total amorality, and an odd laugh. Nobody has seen his eyes behind his black-lensed glasses. His precise realm is uncertain despite the name Tartary. He boasts that his only cooling spring is poisoned [MTM B13:438]. The Argo's investigators include X, Casey Gorshok, Biloxi Brannagan, and Duffey. Casey meets him only through séances, Brannagan searches the shores, and Duffey enters an industrial-agricultural country overlaid by a false desert [MTM B13:438-439]. After temporary escapes into ordinary surroundings, Duffey succumbs to the desert's thirst and drinks from the spring [MTM B13:440-441]. The Prince giggles, and Duffey calls him the Giggling Prince. His immense psychic mentality is contrasted with limited intelligence; his black lenses conceal tiny televisions through which, with his own hallucinations, he experiences the world [MTM B13:441-442]. The water paralyzes Duffey, but the three slant-faced killers actually kill him by cutting away his flesh; a separate trio of slack-faced men burns the remains. When the desert fades, X and Casey recover Duffey's bones and ashes in Gur'yev. The Prince's final fate is unstated [MTM B13:441-442].

MTM B13:437-438; MTM B13:438; MTM B13:438-439; MTM B13:440-441; MTM B13:441-442

Law, TheOne of the three necessities for preserving and rebuilding the world, with worship of God and deeds of kindness and charity. Duffey greatly respects The Law and has a working respect for ordinary laws [MTM B7:228]. The narrative treats Law and worship as congruent under the name Faith, then seeks a synthesis of art as Law, worship, kindness, charity, and creation [MTM B7:229].

MTM B7:228; MTM B7:229

Lawrence SalvatoreFather of Henry Francis Salvatore and husband of Mary Genevieve Hebert, in Henry's Louisiana family [A:122]. Tired of disputes over Henry's schooling, Lawrence examines him, discovers that he is already educated despite considering him the dullest of his boys, and gives him freedom early in his thirteenth year [A:123]. Later he questions Henry's haste to enter the seminary and discusses his reasons and the Church's dangers with him [A:125].

A:122; A:123; A:125

Laycheck, ColonelColonel who, with Majors Meyerhofer, Twicherby, and Terwilliger, reprimands Casey for questioning Stein during an authorized discussion period. None of these officers is a line officer. Laycheck forbids criticism of Stein, threatens a disloyalty charge and ten years, and admits writing Stein's speeches [A:47]. After Casey persuades Stein to prompt a raid on the Australian brigadier through the false Tania story, the scandal brings down Laycheck's star 'like lightning' [A:54].

A:47; A:54

LazarusThe poor man in the parable of the rich man and Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31). Duffey jokingly claims that Dives could have been saved if he had requested a mint julep or Tom Collins rather than water, calling this the test that he failed [A:117].

A:117

Lazarus ReillyProprietor of the Old Wooden Ship. Taking to heart the warning about entertaining angels unawares, he gives newcomers a room, bed, beer credit, and money rather than risk slighting an angel. He says he has much to make up for. The narrator identifies the barmaid Soft-Talk Susie Kutz as the actual angel among the company [D:216]. The hospitality allusion is Hebrews 13:2.

D:216

Le Faye, FatherJesuit and exorcist in Finnegan's account of painting a devil in Florence. He arrives unexpectedly after an overnight train journey, goes directly to the covered picture, recognizes the devil, performs a short exorcism, and orders the painting burned and its ashes swept out [D:254-255]. Van Ghi then identifies the figure as an old repeater in Bruegel, Giotto, El Greco, Notre Dame stonework, Etruscan vases, and Aztec statuettes, and advises Finnegan to paint without inspiration, saying he has drawn the Joker instead of the Queen [D:255].

D:254-255; D:255

Le Marin, CharlesFrench seaman and companion of Finnegan [D:232]. He joins Finnegan, Johnny Duckwalk, and Don Barnaby in their earthly Paradise at Basse-Terre [D:235-237]. His Sarcophagus story alleges that Castleman's men gradually replaced the crew with doubles, including his own replacement at Fort-de-France; he shifts into speaking as one of the raiders, yet says Castleman doubted whether the switch on him had worked. He escapes with valuable contraband and later confronts Castleman [D:243-246]. He eventually leaves Paradise for the sea, saying stomach trouble will not improve until he has a ship beneath him [D:266].

D:232; D:235-237; D:243-246; D:266

Leader, TheCasey Szymansky's first bid for universal power, when he is ten. His Answer proclaims the Leader in a sensational lead article [MTM B4:114]. Medals disappear from Duffey's shop, where he sells residue from Gabriel's former pawn shop [MTM B4:115-116]. An appearance at 7 p.m. beside Henry Horner Park's equestrian statue draws about a hundred thousand people and three bands; a magnificent retired white fire horse waits to be mounted [MTM B4:116-117]. Casey approaches in a scarlet tunic, shako, boots, spurs, belts and bandolier, wearing a hussar sabre and his father's Knights of Columbus sword. His decorations include the Croix de la Legion D'honneur, Croix de Guerre, Medal of Honor, Navy Medal of Honor, Iron Cross, Order of the Golden Fleece medallion, Crown of St. Stephen, Star of the Ninth Fusiliers, and Chicago lodge medals. He says mounting the horse will initiate Plan Beta, taking Chicago, America, and the world [MTM B4:117]. 'Aunt Letitia' intercepts him and makes him pack away the regalia; they go to admire the horse and bands as spectators. The Leader never appears and the Answer ceases. Casey later calls the venture a hoax, but Letitia knows he intended it seriously [MTM B4:117-118].

MTM B4:114; MTM B4:115-116; MTM B4:116-117; MTM B4:117; MTM B4:117-118

Leakley, NellyResident regular at the Old Wooden Ship [D:215]. She is one of the women called salt water widows, whose husbands are seamen [D:221].

D:215; D:221

LearningA recurring practical and spiritual activity. Duffey's school circle is said to live in enterprise, diligence, happiness, learning, and purity [MTM B1:27]. Bagby teaches Duffey to delegate in business, and the two learn to select winds while ballooning [MTM B2:46] [MTM B2:64]. The document collection pairs a warning attributed to Dotty O'Toole's sonnet with Paul's counsel in Philippians 4:4-9 to practice what has been learned [MTM B5:175]. From beyond death Bagby questions whether contentment is something he is meant to learn, while affirming his growing happiness [MTM B8:249]. Duffey rapidly learns and recites his part in Cleo Mahoney's play [MTM B9:265]. In his commentary Stein says exchanging kabouters with Casey has made each privy to the other's secrets [PG:537-538].

MTM B1:27; MTM B2:46; MTM B2:64; MTM B5:175; MTM B8:249; MTM B9:265; PG:537-538

LeavenImage opposed to the lump in Cleo Mahoney's Seven Roads epigraph: 'Be you either lump or leaven' [MTM B10:290]. In 'Great Day,' Duffey rebukes his transformed companions as the lump rather than the leaven, accuses them of failing him, and leaves [GD:495].

MTM B10:290; GD:495

LecturingOne of Special Service Sergeant Absalom Stein's activities. The narrator describes his lectures as plausible and the listeners as uninformed; Casey's questions expose problems, after which the question period is abolished and Casey is reprimanded [A:46-47].

A:46-47

Left Lectionary League, TheOrganization honored with sacrifices of goats among the broad assortment of offerings at the Conclave in Babylonia Bagascia [MB:565-566].

MB:565-566

Left-handedFinnegan's teasing description of Australian table manners. Tom Shire explains that Australians keep the knife in the right hand and fork in the left, while Americans transfer the fork after cutting [A:4]. In a separate notebook entry Casey describes left- and right-handed rocks according to formation and cleavage [A:164].

A:4; A:164

Leftfooted killerUnidentified pursuer asking for Finnegan in Florida. Finnegan says that the man wants to kill him on an earlier assignment, unrelated to the latest trouble [D:182-183]. After another inquiry in Winter Garden, the killer and a companion follow Finnegan, who has departed in the Georgia Kiunker; they do not ride in his car [D:193]. Under repeated fire, Finnegan ditches the Klunker and disables the pursuing car, then wounds both men as they flee [D:197].

D:182-183; D:193; D:197

Legends of the Persian GulfWork credited to Moisha El-Gazma in the epigraph to 'The Wives of Sindbad.' Its account imagines Bassorah as a fire-scarred rock slab in muddy shallows, perhaps once a launching pad for space fleets, and invokes a missing Night about Sindbads trading between worlds [D:53].

D:53

LegionThe Pop Countess's answer both to Duffey's question about the number of her people and to Stein's question about the name of her society and principality [MTM B11:319]. It echoes Mark 5:9 and Luke 8:30, where the possessing spirit or possessed man answers Jesus with the name Legion because the demons are many.

MTM B11:319

Leonardo da Vinci (1452--1519)Italian Renaissance artist and investigator of anatomy, engineering, mechanics, and flight, whose paintings include The Last Supper and Mona Lisa. Jimmy Fitzjames says a newly discovered Leonardo would bring a hundred thousand dollars and claims Adam Scanlon is better [A:230]. The narrator calls Scanlon possibly as good as Leonardo and likens their habit of painting while talking to an audience; it is the narrator, not Scanlon, who calls Adam the better talker [A:233-234]. Casey's notebook XXXII attributes to Leonardo a question about rivers becoming deeper and clearer after a great pestilence, then mocks it as an example of a great man's silliness [A:165].

A:230; A:233-234; A:165

Les Cent Nouvelles nouvellesThe fifteenth-century French collection Les Cent Nouvelles nouvelles, or One Hundred New Tales, here printed as 'Les Cents Novelles Nouvelles.' Hans buys it at a New York secondhand bookstall after giving a young scholar a quarter for Jaufre and Brunissende [A:224]. The scholar introduces himself as James Fitzjames on the following page [A:225].

A:224; A:225

Les Cents Novelle NouvellesEarlier heading differed from both the standard title and the novel’s printed Les Cents Novelles Nouvelles. See Les Cent Nouvelles nouvelles.
Les Contes DrolatiquesRibald tales by Honoré de Balzac (1799-1850), first published in collections between 1832 and 1837. A favorite of Gautier the goat-man, who reads French books aloud to his goats on winter nights in the Harlow House library; he says that Balzac appeals to goats and to the goat in man [A:196-198].

A:196-198

Lessing, MiriamMother of Casey Szymansky and wife of Gabriel Szymansky, the pawnbroker and antique dealer. Casey is their only child, born in Chicago on October 7, 1921 [A:153-154].

A:153-154

Letters After I am DeadWork attributed to Bascom Bagby in an epigraph. It proposes Iron Meadows inhabited by Aspects and says some aspects of the Argo Legend dwell in a meadow unknown to both God and Duffey [MTM B5:177].

MTM B5:177

LevantThe eastern Mediterranean region. Professor Kirol von Weinsberg-Valeni is said to know all the tongues of Europe and the Levant, as well as the world's important languages [A:213].

A:213

LeviathanBiblical sea monster, notably in Job 41, Psalm 74:14 and Isaiah 27:1. Casey reports Duffey's political analogy: liberals formerly wanted Leviathan only a little larger than the other whales, but now want it to devour them [A:42]. In Trinali Peterson's image for the Elephants' Graveyard, the largest driftwood becomes the bones of Leviathan, older than elephants, mammoths and behemoths [A:232]. Leviathans graze in the salt-water portions of Zabotski Flats, and leviathan steak appears in the children's grace at Zabotski's floating dinner table alongside hippopotamus, rhinoceros, behemoth, alligator, buffalo, elephant and green turtle [MTM B12:362-363].

A:42; A:232; MTM B12:362-363

Leviathan, Edward CardinalCardinal of Edinburgh, one of the thirteen primaries on John Mogul's list. His double is Douglas McAfee of London [MB:579].

MB:579

LevinAn archaic word for lightning. In the 'Ici Parle Isolde' section of Casey's youthful ballad, the levin 'dances fire' beneath grumbling clouds [A:152-153].

A:152-153

Levine y O'Brien, GilbertoRio double of Carlos Cardinal Artemis of Santa Cruz [MB:579]. After the thirteen primaries have been killed, Gilberto, Finnegan and Herman Hercules travel aboard the Argo; all thirteen shadows are still alive at this stage [MB:589]. Their masked, skeletal pilot is Melchisedech [MB:590]. Gilberto fears that the identifying marks he made on his own skin may have been forged, and refuses Finnegan's offer to inspect them. This uncertainty is separate from Finnegan's secret masterpiece imprinted inside Artemis's skin: the narrative leaves open whether that painting is inside Gilberto's present skin or the flayed trophy possessed by John Mogul [MB:590-591].

MB:579; MB:589; MB:590; MB:590-591

LevitesMembers of the Israelite tribe of Levi, assigned to assist the priesthood in Numbers 3:6-10. In the Rounders' Club farewell scene, the narrator includes 'priests and Levites' among the city's people who come to honor Duffey [MTM B2:70].

MTM B2:70

Lewis, Don (Timothy Lorrigan)Brunhilde crewman, dark and exceptionally handsome, who shares a cabin with Finnegan and Joe Cross and belongs to the narrative's 'good people' [D:30-31]. His campfire story identifies him indirectly as PFC Timothy Lorrigan: with Sergeant Charles Santee and Corporal Robert Casper he disappeared from patrol on Pulau Petir, or Willy Jones Island, on October 1, 1944. After the other two kill the elusive man called Yokipoki, Lorrigan buries him; apparently resurrected movement proves to be rats at the body [D:44-47]. Despite calling himself a coward, Don secretly organizes resistance aboard the Brunhilde, brings Joe, Manuel, Anastasia and Finnegan into the affair, communicates toward the Devil's resurrection without understanding a critical part of it, and tips the balance so Finnegan lives and Dopey dies [D:105]. Hunted in Tangier, he finds Seaworthy at the consulate and cannot buy refuge from the man who hides fugitives [D:106-108]. Marie Courtois kills him by throttling him and breaking his neck. Finnegan finds him in a weed patch, laments how little he knew his friend, and buries him in clean sand beneath aromatic creepers [D:109-110] [D:112-113]. Later an unidentified dead man's voice comes from the sleeping Don Barnaby's hammock and asks Finnegan to repay Anastasia fifty dollars; the episode suggests a return of Don Lewis without naming the voice [D:238].

D:30-31; D:44-47; D:105; D:106-108; D:109-110; D:112-113; D:238

Lewis, Jake (Jake-Leg)Old Wooden Ship associate and salt-water cowboy. Jake-Leg Lewis and Tommy Cow-Town Borger ride cattle boats, not horses, but always wear boots, spurs, chaps and gauntlets; dwindling live-cattle shipments leave long intervals between voyages [D:215-216] [D:222]. His nickname may allude to 'Jake leg,' the gait impairment caused by adulterated Jamaica ginger consumed during Prohibition, though the novel does not explain his nickname or diagnose him.

D:215-216; D:222

Li Tai PoChinese poet of the Tang period (701-762), also known as Li Po. In Hans Schultz's unpublished ballad he sings while playing the flute, turns youthful heartbreak into songs of kings and working people, drinks, and joins a fisher maid in her boat. After telling her he loved her in another form long ago, he tumbles into the water and drowns [A:221-223].

A:221-223

Liberal CatholicThe description Casey plans to give the Crock as a vehicle for 'Their' handouts and quotations, according to Mary Catherine Carruthers. She regards his continued membership in the Church as making him more valuable to his new associates [A:98].

A:98

LiberalsA recurrent target of the characters' political and religious polemic. Casey reports Duffey's accusation that collectivists have appropriated the name, reversed liberal preferences from minimal to maximal government, and allowed only one creed of thought; Casey himself remarks that Duffey's analogies are difficult [A:42]. Henry Salvatore describes a Secular-Liberal Religion working inside the Church, and Patrick Stranahan denounces secular-liberal influence as an internal parasite [A:125] [A:110]. Bascom Bagby names Secular Liberalism among seven heads of the enemy, with Dialectic Materialism, Artistic Degradation, Judas Priestism, Panaceic Pentecostalism, Murderous Molochism and Atheistic Communism [MTM B5:169]. X's account of the Devil's Crimean release describes the Liberal Consensus and the intelligentsia as disproportionately represented among the attendees [MTM B6:204-205].

A:42; A:125; A:110; MTM B5:169; MTM B6:204-205

Lien of Extreme NeedFinnegan's purported common-law justification for possessing a commandeered car 'for a while.' He offers the phrase when the girl driving it suspects that neither the money he gives her nor the car is honestly his [D:168].

D:168

LifeDuffey's overlapping lives organize the narrative introduced as a magus's daily life. He remembers three contemporaneous childhoods and an older, continuing existence; the Boy King's life is presented as more substantial than its later shadows [MTM B1:5-6] [MTM B1:17]. His analyst interprets part of his childhood as a girl's life, while his mind-piracy lets him appropriate other people's experiences, including Sebastian's youthful countess affair [MTM B1:16] [MTM B1:31]. The narrator jokes about Sebastian's apparently short-lived appearance, treats education as an ultimate passion, and makes art expertise a lifelong Duffey vocation [MTM B1:22] [MTM B1:29] [MTM B1:34]. A watershed dream anticipates Duffey's departure; his seven hidden years are compared with supposed gaps in famous lives and yield seven Christ artworks and remembered loves he cannot revisit [MTM B2:68] [MTM B2:72] [MTM B3:103] [MTM B4:110]. Zabotski says years in the Pristine World can fill a day or two in the Molasses World [MTM B9:279]. Duffey recalls coming ashore in 1923 into a young life he can choose again; the long-lived Argo pilots owe extraordinary service, and the Sea of the Seven Lost Years joins nonconsecutive times and shores [MTM B12:370] [MTM B13:405-406]. His death, ashes and living flesh coexist; returning through an earlier shore restores the life ahead of him. Later he emerges aged twenty-three after seven variant lives and deaths, yet even the reality of his lives is questioned in his conversation with little Teresa [MTM B13:445] [MTM B13:465] [MTM B13:472]. Related treatments include Hilary Hilton's accusation that Casey flees life and reality, the Casey Machines' invasive experiences across death, and Finnegan's painting of his own aged resurrection [PG:531] [CM:507-509] [MB:551]. In 'Great Day,' remaining persons and verses must be disposed of before the world's conclusion; in 'How Many Miles to Babylon,' the Covenant is called the world's life-line [GD:501] [MB:594].

MTM B1:5-6; MTM B1:17; MTM B1:16; MTM B1:31; MTM B1:22; MTM B1:29; MTM B1:34; MTM B2:68; MTM B2:72; MTM B3:103; MTM B4:110; MTM B9:279; MTM B12:370; MTM B13:405-406; MTM B13:445; MTM B13:465; MTM B13:472; PG:531; CM:507-509; MB:551; GD:501; MB:594

Lightfoot, MaryOne of Duffey's Chicago friends, listed with the college and university people, and wife of Isaac Lightfoot [MTM B3:99] [MTM B4:130]. A peacemaker during the argument about moving the mule, she urges Duffey to let the 'blow-mouths' grow until the final harvest separates them from good people [MTM B4:130]. She appears with Duffey in a compromisingly presented photograph [MTM B4:139]. Both Lightfoots attend the great farewell gathering at which Duffey sees his old friends for the last time in normal flesh [MTM B12:383].

MTM B3:99; MTM B4:130; MTM B4:139; MTM B12:383

LilithLilith, the woman created alongside Adam in the Alphabet of Ben Sira's alternative-wife tradition. In Hans's reflections on Marie's eyes, 'Lillith who was before Eve' is called a witch and therefore green-eyed, giving green-eyed women primogeniture [A:24].

A:24

LillithLillith is the spelling printed in the novel for Lilith. See Lilith.
LimitThe first item in the good column of the Pythagorean table described in Casey's biography, opposed to the unlimited in the evil column [A:154]. Aristotle's Metaphysics 986a likewise places limit and unlimited in opposing columns aligned with good and bad.

A:154

Lincoln, Abraham (1809--1865)Sixteenth president of the United States (1809-1865), who led the Union during the Civil War, issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863, and articulated the war's democratic purpose in the Gettysburg Address. The narrator includes Lincoln among historical figures supposedly possessing seven hidden or dark years, as a parallel for Duffey's missing years [MTM B2:72].

MTM B2:72

Lines in Her Duffey Book (by Mary Virginia Schaeffer)Mary Virginia Schaeffer's speculative account of Duffey as a visitor from one of nine discarded worlds preceding the present tenth world. She expressly admits that the idea has no scriptural or revelatory authority. In her conjecture those worlds remain inhabited, and Duffey's genius, lack of parents and endless circular life derive from another world's conditions. She anticipates his collision with this world and his scattering into seven voyages [MTM B10:291-292].

MTM B10:291-292

Lines Written in Margin of Perrone's Praelectiones TheologicaeMargaret Stone's note asking whether Duffey, pulled back after reaching his own edge of time, has drawn his companions back within the same fabric of time. The preceding year feels to her as though it has been lived several times; Salvation Sally reports the same sensation [MTM B10:291].

MTM B10:291

LingoFinnegan's speech includes Little Italy dialects unintelligible in the next street [A:6]. Anastasia's sarcastic account of Marie Courtois says she 'tosses the lingo' [D:33]. In the account of Duffey's animated creations, sorcerers call their smoky halo the 'unreality fringe' [MTM B5:158].

A:6; D:33; MTM B5:158

LinusSt. Peter's immediate successor as bishop of Rome. The Vatican lists his pontificate as 68-79, although early chronologies differ. Irenaeus says the apostles entrusted the episcopate to Linus and identifies him with the Linus of 2 Timothy 4:21. His traditional martyrdom is historically uncertain; he is named in the Roman Canon, and his feast is September 23. In Henry's dream, Linus, Clement and Cletus are among the crew of the Navicula Petri, whose sailors may be dolls or living people [A:44-45].

A:44-45

Lion of the SouthJimmy Hansen's announced title for Joe Bushmaster in the world championship beer-drinking contest against Hans Schultz, the Milwaukee Seidel [A:19].

A:19

LisbonCity that may still be looking at its bay in Finnegan's travel poem, which begins 'I'll drive me a boat'; Dotty finds the verses among Finnegan's papers [A:171-173]. Johnny Duckwalk cannot remember whether he met Kristine in Lisbon or Stockholm [D:246].

A:171-173; D:246

Little Alcohol (John Indelecio)John Indelecio, a burglar and regular at the Old Wooden Ship [D:215]. He does the climbing and high-window work, while his partner John (Big Alcohol) Jereboam handles drills, saws, chisels and pry-bars. They work only when deeply in debt to Lazarus Reilly [D:218].

D:215; D:218

Little Daisey Pancake TurnersOne thousand gross of pancake turners peddled by Hillary Hilton and Finnegan, along with four carloads of acid, before planned dealings in a bridge and distressed cigars [A:253].

A:253

Little Dotty NesbittOld Wooden Ship regular [D:215], one of four Dottys whose identities and marriages Finnegan finds confusing: Nesbitt, Danvers, Peisson and Hulme. Little Dotty and Dotty Danvers married two brothers in Sugarland, Texas; one of those brothers had also married Dotty Hulme [D:220]. Little Dotty's first husband and an earlier husband of Dotty Danvers had the same name, which does not by itself establish that they were the same man [D:221].

D:215; D:220; D:221

Little Dutch EckelEngineer at a Texas City refinery who still lives at the Old Wooden Ship because its people let him stay when he was poor. Now the 'prince of the place,' he spends more there than anyone else [D:221].

D:221

Little Fat-HeadOne of the familiar valleys Don Lewis names while recalling how he, Santee, and Casper became lost after Yokipoki’s killing. He says that they knew these named valleys, but did not recognize the valley they were in [D:45-46].

D:45-46

Little ItalyA source of the mixed dialects in Finnegan's speech: his 'Little Italy lingos' are unintelligible in the next street [A:6].

A:6

Little Joker CanyonOne of the familiar valleys in Don Lewis’s account of the patrol on Willy Jones Island. The soldiers know its name, but cannot identify the valley in which they become lost after Yokipoki’s killing [D:45-46].

D:45-46

“Little Looking Glass”The title Finnegan recalls, tentatively as Specchietto, from an Italian reader. A boy lends his face to the figure in his little mirror; the mirror boy also borrows his shadow and name and never gives them back. The original boy remains invisible in a dark corner. Finnegan identifies himself with him, reduced to a comic mask, a monicker and the shadow of a shadow [A:55-56].

A:55-56

Little Miss ResurrectionFinnegan's name for Anastasia Demetriades. After she washes and shaves him and treats his injuries, he associates her name with resurrection and his restored respectability [D:16]. He later addresses her as 'Little Miss Resurrection' while reminding her to love her enemies [D:33].

D:16; D:33

Little Oyster Bar, TheEstablishment called the Little Oyster where Finnegan wins eight hundred dollars at dice during an interval when the world seems newly interesting to him [D:20].

D:20

Little Road CrawlerCar Finnegan wants to buy. Doll proposes adding it to the Celestial Omnibus and Georgia Kiunker, then drawing lots for the three cars and scattering in different directions [D:185]. The later departure scene calls Doll's car the Road Runner; the passage does not establish that this is a separate fourth vehicle [D:193].

D:185; D:193

Living GothicThe architectural metaphor applied to Gertrude Brannagan, a style to which Finnegan is partial. About forty-five, with fifteen years' leeway either way, she is full-built, pretty, dark and 'frenchy,' with curly hair and a smile; the narrator likens her volutes and parapets to a fortress [D:200].

D:200

Livy (Titus Livius) (64/59 BC--17 AD)Roman historian, born in 64 or 59 BCE and traditionally dated to 17 CE at his death, though 12 CE is another proposed date. His Ab Urbe Condita traces Rome from its legendary foundation to 9 BCE; thirty-five of its 142 books survive complete. Its treatment of civic and personal virtue helped shape later readings of Roman history, including Renaissance literature and political thought. Patrick Stranahan considers Livy sufficient for Latin and, with Cobbett, history [A:109].

A:109

Lloyd-Spencer, David CardinalCardinal of Cardiff, one of the targets named in John Mogul's thirteen-man assassination contract [MB:571]. The primary-double list pairs him with 'Llyod CardiganPembroke of Tywyn' [MB:579], although the later narrative calls Lloyd Cardigan-Pembroke the double of Cardinal Ti, an inconsistency in the text [MB:594].

MB:571; MB:579; MB:594

Locke, John (1632--1704)English philosopher and physician (1632-1704), a major exponent of empiricism and liberal political thought. An Essay Concerning Human Understanding makes experience central to knowledge; Two Treatises of Government develops natural rights, consent and the limits of political authority. These works became central to Enlightenment philosophy and later democratic thought. In notebook XXXIV, the schoolboy Casey admits that a supposed howler in Locke ceased to look like one after he read further and understood it better [A:166].

A:166

LogorrheaExcessive use of words. Sergeant Kelly regards Howell in Ward Fourteen as moderately sane apart from his logorrhea; the narrator adds that Howell talks a lot [A:75-76]. Finnegan also gets logorrhea when he is drinking and celebrating St. Patrick's Day [D:189].

A:75-76; D:189

Lost Years (The SevenDuffey's seven years aboard the Argo, beginning when he boards the disguised ship below the Eads Bridge in St. Louis during his fifth or sixth youth. The years are not consecutive: land adventures are excluded from the count and do not reduce his lifespan [MTM B2:71] [MTM B13:406]. They mix past, present and future in intervals held apart from ordinary time, sometimes revisitable without fracturing reality [MTM B10:298]. In their own context they are the Seven Golden Years; the Fourteenth Voyage belongs to them and is certain to occur, without excluding other contingencies [MTM B10:300]. Duffey obtains the Seven Christs in these years and remembers women he says he cannot revisit [MTM B3:103] [MTM B4:110]. During the hidden years, before Casey's conception, he gives Gabriel Szymansky Casey's talisman; other talismans are bestowed during or possibly before them [MTM B4:120-121]. Bagby somehow sends weekly letters throughout Duffey's absence, and later compares Duffey's fractured, adolescent state with his condition during the Lost Years [MTM B4:145] [MTM B10:302]. When the seven-arrowed sign blocks an ordinary future, Duffey can proceed only through their unusual context [MTM B10:290]. The Sea of the Seven Lost Years has scattered channels and shores and connects to the Sea of Amnesia by a hidden strait [MTM B13:406]. Later Duffey can re-enter from shores at different ages, become young aboard ship and leave through an earlier shore with his long life still ahead [MTM B13:445].

MTM B2:71; MTM B13:406; MTM B10:298; MTM B10:300; MTM B3:103; MTM B4:110; MTM B4:120-121; MTM B4:145; MTM B10:302; MTM B10:290; MTM B13:445

LoveAffection, desire, family attachment and compassion recur in overlapping forms. Duffey and Lily Koch love each other, though Lily directs him toward her sister Letitia [MTM B1:30] [MTM B3:90]. Duffey declares love for Gretchen Sisler, almost nine, while he is almost sixteen; Evelyn London calls him her boy and her love [MTM B2:39-40]. He feels sudden, frightening love for Mary Louise Byrne, called his sister, consort and an exteriorized part of himself; their actual kinship remains uncertain. Beth Keegan declares love at their first meeting, Mary Louise says their whole circle loves one another, and Beth calls Charley Murray her second love [MTM B2:55-56] [MTM B2:60] [MTM B2:67]. Duffey also declares love for nine-year-old Charlotte Mullens [MTM B3:78]. Letitia tells Duffey that he already loves her as they arrange their marriage; August Koch's concern for Lily expresses a father's love [MTM B3:91-92] [MTM B3:102]. Duffey's affections extend to Letitia, Lily, Elinore Koch, women in St. Louis and the unrevisitable loves of his hidden years [MTM B4:110]. Patrick Stranahan and Duffey love Teresa Piccone [MTM B5:163]. The narrator describes Hans as loving everyone, with a particular affection for Trinali Peterson [A:224]; Finnegan's resolve to avenge Anastasia follows the loss of the person he loves best [D:157-158]. Paul’s exhortation to dwell on things loved and honored appears among the guiding documents [MTM B5:175]. In the Casey commentaries, Demetrio Glauch questions whether extreme compassion for the Devil has become sinful; Hilary Hilton reluctantly obeys the sign that Casey must be loved and describes Casey's love of farce. Finnegan affirms Casey's genuine compassion for vulnerable creatures and natural beauty while lamenting its misdirection toward a powerful monster [PG:518-519] [PG:531-532] [PG:543-544].

MTM B1:30; MTM B3:90; MTM B2:39-40; MTM B2:55-56; MTM B2:60; MTM B2:67; MTM B3:78; MTM B3:91-92; MTM B3:102; MTM B4:110; MTM B5:163; A:224; D:157-158; MTM B5:175; PG:518-519; PG:531-532; PG:543-544

LoyaltyThe Fiefdoms maintain an uneven loyalty in the struggle against the world's enemy, while Absalom Stein is absolutely loyal to ordered, structured arts [MTM B8:246]. X compares the Devil's awaiting servants with the loyal subjects of enchanted kings who expect their return [MTM B6:205]. Gautier's seven youngest goat kids share loyalty to the ideal of climbing a fallen sycamore [A:194]. Colonel Laycheck threatens to charge Casey with disloyalty and impose ten years if he continues opposing Stein's instruction [A:47]. X also speculates that Ifreann Gregorovitch may have felt loyalty to the Krakow region, despite his rebellion against authority and opportunistic appeals to patriotism [D:280].

MTM B8:246; MTM B6:205; A:194; A:47; D:280

Lsuno CollegeNew Orleans institution where Danny Degas is a history professor [MTM B11:322]. The name points to LSUNO, Louisiana State University in New Orleans, the institution subsequently known as the University of New Orleans.

MTM B11:322

LuinLuin, or Monday, one of Gautier's seven youngest goat kids. She alone cannot climb the fallen sycamore until Finnegan gives her a boost, and the others acknowledge his help [A:194-196].

A:194-196

LuluwayJoseph's correction of Finnegan's 'lulus' as the plural for diamonds. Joseph says Finnegan will learn the word and must develop his own smuggling technique rather than copy another man's [D:95].

D:95

LupidoCafe proprietor who favors candlelight. He gives Trinali Peterson stubs after burning the candles only partway down, and she steals longer candles from him. He also supplies her with old bread and leftover wine [A:228]. When her landlord cuts off the heat and she barricades herself in her room to resist eviction, she lowers a basket from the window and Lupido feeds her through it. Her 'old moustache' is Lupido himself, not a name for the bread [A:229].

A:228; A:229

Luther, MartinGerman theologian (1483-1546) and leading figure of the Protestant Reformation. In the fictional epigraph from Carmody Overlark's Studies in the imagination, Luther appears with Plato, Homer, Aquinas, Rabelais, Smart, Rasputin, Toussaint L'Ouverture and Steinmetz among people alleged to have a Neanderthal-type head. The passage associates its low brow and enlarged back-brain with unusual imagination, spiritual gifts and criminality [D:270-272].

D:270-272

LuzonThe largest Philippine island. After the Second World War, the Dirty Five wait there for a ship home with no duties, expecting to leave in about a month; Hans reproaches Finnegan for his red eyes [A:63]. They drink with Captain Sammy Guiterrez at the Buffalo Bar [A:66]. Hans knows of two white horses nearby and subsequently rides the stallion as part of the group's Argonautic play [A:68].

A:63; A:66; A:68

Lynne, Janeway CelesteJaneway Celeste Lynne, one of three twenty-one-year-old cousins who arrive by rowboat in waterlogged rural Louisiana during the Argo’s visit, only two and a half minutes after Honeybucket Kincaid activates his frequency apparatus [MTM B13:416-419]. She says that an extraordinary tide seemed to catch their boat and propel it along. Duffey points out that they came against the ocean tide and attributes their movement to Honeybucket Kincaid’s frequency modulation. Introducing herself as Janeway, she names her cousins Candy Sue Pirogue and Etta Mae Mansion to the company, which includes Leonard Archive, Duffey and Biloxi Brannagan [MTM B13:416-419].

MTM B13:416-419

LynxAnimal in a quotation Casey attributes to Aristotle in notebook XXXIII: the lynx supposedly hides its urine because people use it for purposes including signets. Casey calls this one of Aristotle's better observations [A:165-166]. A closely corresponding ancient account occurs in Theophrastus's On Stones, section28, where lyngourion used for seals is connected with concealed animal urine; this is a historical belief about a supposed stone, not established lynx biology.

A:165-166

LyonesseLegendary lost land off Cornwall. During Hans Schultz’s New York period, the narrator describes the city as more than Baghdad, Paris, Heidelberg, and Lyonesse [A:224].

A:224

MSee Melchisedech Duffey.
Machiavelli, Niccolò (1469--1527)Italian political writer, author of The Prince (1532). Machiavelli is among the writers whose ideas Casey mixes into The Answer; the narration places his contributions among the newspaper’s worse borrowings [MTM B4:114] [MTM B4:118].

MTM B4:114; MTM B4:118

Madame Le MourcheorMaker of Old Original Juju Joy Pills in New Orleans. Don Barnaby praises her recipe of frankincense-tree sawdust, honey from the meadows around Megapolis in Arcady, and a black cat with glanders. He says she omits the fanciful additives used by other makers, including a red-eyed goat’s stomach stone and a swamp dragon’s blood [D:249].

D:249

Mae (Old Wooden Ship)One of the women living at the Old Wooden Ship who are called “salt water widows.” She is also named in its roster of resident regulars [D:216] [D:221].

D:216; D:221

Mae, EttaEarlier incomplete heading, which treated Mae as the surname. See Mansion, Etta Mae.
Magellan, Ferdinand (c. 1480--1521)Portuguese navigator whose Spanish expedition of 1519–1522 made the first circumnavigation of the globe. Magellan died in the Philippines in 1521, before the voyage was completed. Dotty invokes him when she teases Finnegan for not knowing whether he has been around the world; Finnegan replies that Magellan was in command and he was not [A:145].

A:145

Magic LanternAnastasia’s assembly of reflecting mirrors and a lantern, housed in an old boat’s binnacle case. Explicitly distinguished from a projector, it accompanies her and Finnegan’s nighttime vigil [D:131].

D:131

Magkaano ito?Finnegan’s Tagalog question about the price of liquor at Falo and Nauti’s unfinished cabaret. Nauti answers that it costs a peso a bottle because they are the first customers [A:64].

A:64

MagnesiteMaterial that Casey’s seventh high-school notebook entry says is used chiefly to make refractory bricks for furnace linings [A:162-163].

A:162-163

MagnificaAdmiring Spanish exclamation directed at Marie Courtois by a man ashore on the Mexican side. When Anastasia tells him that Marie can carry a man on her shoulders, he answers “Interesante” [D:57].

D:57

MagpieBird loved and married by Amoy during his supposed life as a red-winged blackbird and jewel thief. Ignatius Ti calls her a common magpie, but Amoy protests and Ti interprets his words as meaning an uncommon individual of the common species [A:80].

A:80

MagusMagician or sorcerer, the role of Melchisedech Duffey. The opening describes his many mantles of magic and foretells their loss; his strongest gift is manufacturing persons, or marking unfinished human clay with his fabricator’s mark [MTM B1:5]. He summons an invisible giant’s hand to ring a bell [MTM B1:15], and his school confessor accepts his vocation while warning him against pride [MTM B1:28]. Casey is named one of his creations [MTM B4:118]. Duffey defends his powers against Doctor Morris Poor [MTM B4:128], though Margaret Stone calls him a “moth-eaten sorcerer” [MTM B4:112]. He produces a living mouse after offering, without certainty that he can do so, to produce a dinosaur [MTM B5:170]. The Loosed Devil seeks his creative services; Duffey asserts that he actually creates and refuses compulsion [MTM B10:302-303]. Later the magus recognizes himself as Melchisedech, King of Salem, called Duffey in latter-day contexts [MTM B13:402].

MTM B1:5; MTM B1:15; MTM B1:28; MTM B4:118; MTM B4:128; MTM B4:112; MTM B5:170; MTM B10:302-303; MTM B13:402

Mahoney, CleoUrsuline Academy student and playwright of Seven Roads. She is among the girls who explain the painted sign “The Future Begins Right Here,” gives Duffey the script, and describes its problem: what happens when Melchisedech, who cannot have an ending, reaches the end of the world [MTM B9:264-265]. At the Ghost Coffee Shop she calls the roads seven scenarios or variant futures, selected through encounters with particular potholes [MTM B10:293]. She describes the play as a study of frustrations [MTM B10:297]. Later she supplies revised lines that strengthen its Fifth Road, in which she plays the Hoyden [MTM B12:352].

MTM B9:264-265; MTM B10:293; MTM B10:297; MTM B12:352

Main Frequency ModulatorFirst frequency modulator, linked to all the others. Duffey dives head-first into it while Biloxi Brannagan prevents interference. Lightning and a stench follow; Duffey emerges with his clothing and body hair burned off. He says he has abolished the Puff Fish frequency in past, present, and future without breaking the apparatus [MTM B13:420].

MTM B13:420

MainlandMain body of land, opposed to an island. In her dispute with Hans and Marie about religious authority, Salvation Sally invokes island dwellers; Hans supplies their insistence that their island is the mainland, and Sally suggests the analogy may apply to her Catholic listeners [A:8].

A:8

Majesty, TheTitle prescribed for the Devil at the New Catholic Press Guild meeting. The introducer calls the being an androgyne beyond grammar and directs that it be adored by snickering [MTM B8:239-240]. Its human appearance conceals a giant whose mind Duffey enters [MTM B8:240-241]. That mind declares its aim of undoing Creation through hatred, conspiracy, slander, disorder, and final nullity [MTM B8:242]. “Holding More Meaningful Liturgical Services” disguises its promised “Devouring of Entrails in the Holy Places.” Duffey finds that the public speech and the interior speech convey the same message beneath different vocabulary [MTM B8:243].

MTM B8:239-240; MTM B8:240-241; MTM B8:242; MTM B8:243

Maker ManTeresa Piccone Stranahan’s name for Duffey in a private letter. She says he lacks firsthand knowledge of the experiences she describes, instead raiding other people’s minds and pretending to have known their contents already: “That Maker Man, he just doesn’t have it” [MTM B6:188].

MTM B6:188

Malaki ibon“Big bird,” the self-description of the small parakeet Amoy in the narrative’s Tagalog-Parakeet language [A:79].

A:79

Malay boyBoy who enters the hospital ward, calls the amnesiac Sergeant by name, and tells him it is time to go home. The pair then find themselves in Sydney, where the boy leaves him at the Plaza Hotel to visit old friends [A:88]. Back in the islands, they dive from a canoe named Aral, Bumi, and Aragh, which the Sergeant recognizes as the Argo [A:89].

A:88; A:89

Malay boy (2)Uncertain entry. The cited Tangier episode describes a little Arab boy who organizes runners for Finnegan, but does not identify a Malay boy among them [D:104].

D:104

MalayaRegion off which, in Finnegan’s account of island origins, a bronze bowl broke into long pieces that became islands [A:35].

A:35

Malayan dialectWhat the outsiders called Gorgios mistake for the speech taught to islanders called Jojos. Finnegan explains that the Dirty Five taught them Polish while the Jojos themselves believed it was English [A:73].

A:73

MaleficentThe harmful or evil side in Papa Devil’s formula for the struggle: the old game of monsters and men, policemen and thieves, the Beneficient and the Maleficent [D:120].

D:120

Maliit ibon“Little bird,” the name the parakeet Amoy angrily rejects with “hindi, hindi.” The narration glosses his reply as “no, no, no” [A:79].

A:79

MalmoMalmö, the Swedish city. The poem opening Finnegan’s chapter says that Malmo is crisp in the fall [A:171-172].

A:171-172

MaloryOne of the surnames used by Gregory McColum Papadiabolous, the Irish Papa Devil or Papadiabolous II, according to X [D:285].

D:285

Mamma MonicaNarrator’s designation for Monica Stranahan as she asks Maurine to help with Vincent and Theresa’s wedding arrangements [A:104-105].

A:104-105

MammonWealth personified as an object of worship. At Babylonia Bagascia, the Unilateral Workers’ League receives a money offering and enthrones its Mammon statue during the ceremonies outside Conclave Hall [MB:566].

MB:566

Man from Minneapolis, TheOne of Endymeon Ellenbogen’s three published novels, financed through subsidy presses. Endymeon claims that his novels have been solid successes with the people who count, while wondering whether he can afford further such successes [A:237].

A:237

Man of MysteryCode name for the Antichrist whom the three Argo Masters try to keep from boarding their ship [MTM B13:454] [MTM B13:456]. He is subsequently manifested as Kasmir Gorshok, Prince Casimir, Casey Szymansky, and Peleus, within a future whose shimmering marks its lack of absolute finality [MTM B13:454] [MTM B13:462].

MTM B13:454; MTM B13:456; MTM B13:462

Man-killing pantherPanther in Finnegan’s catalogue of the terrors of the Chosky Bottoms, a legendary spook place said to be just beyond the next ridge [D:274].

D:274

Man-sized germBiloxi Brannagan’s image for the agent of the world’s recurring “brain damage.” He calls it a parasite, “the alien within,” and fears it will destroy both its host and itself [D:202-203].

D:202-203

Mandarin picture (Adam Scanlon might sell)Adam Scanlon painting recommended by Jimmy when Hans proposes furnishing his flat in the Chinese style. Jimmy jokes that Scanlon might accept a thousand dollars, then discusses a price nearer fifteen. Hans answers that for a thousand dollars he would paint a Mandarin himself [A:229-230].

A:229-230

Manford, PhilipYoung man from the school of music who accompanies Duffey on outings with Mary Louise and Beth Keegan in St. Louis. They sometimes use Manford’s Overland automobile for rides, dinner, and theatre visits [MTM B2:58].

MTM B2:58

ManilaCity to which the group travels by truck after supper on New Year’s Eve. Just after midnight they begin boarding the ship for home [A:70].

A:70

ManoloCharlotte Mullens’s son, who accompanies her and Gloria Mullens to Duffey’s north-side Chicago hotel [MTM B3:81]. When Duffey suggests that her son and sister are projections or ventriloquist’s figures, Charlotte explains that she uses pliable flesh-and-blood people to make compliant figures [MTM B3:83]. In Duffey’s nocturnal vision, she commands Manolo and Gloria to stop the stevedore attacking him [MTM B3:85]. Manolo and Gloria are later found tortured and murdered in the hotel; Letitia says the killers sought information the pair did not possess [MTM B3:97].

MTM B3:81; MTM B3:83; MTM B3:85; MTM B3:97

Mansion, Etta MaeEtta Mae Mansion, cousin of Janeway Celeste Lynne and Candy Sue Pirogue. The three twenty-one-year-old women arrive by rowboat after Honeybucket Kincaid activates frequencies intended to attract them [MTM B13:419].

MTM B13:419

Mansions (in Father's House)John 14:2 allusion in the Professor’s account of Heaven and his own return to the Church. He assures Hans that the Father’s House has mansions even for charlatans [A:214-215].

A:214-215

Mansville Burgess HowlandBrother named by Howland Jerome Howland when he tells Finnegan about his father, John Commodore Howland, and his seven brothers. Their father gave them names from old families he disliked, apparently to irritate those families [A:178].

A:178

Mantles of magicDuffey’s initial abundance of magical gifts, most of which he is expected to lose. The opening enumerates his production of gold, invasion of minds, limited movement through time, command of invisible giants, and fabrication of persons [MTM B1:5].

MTM B1:5

ManuelStowaway and self-declared spy aboard the Brunhilde [D:54]. He comes from farther south than Mexico and seeks the source of a power turning men into devils; he fears that Papa Devil will kill him [D:56]. After the Naxos fighting, he is alive and crying when Finnegan meets him. The two leave the dead behind and hide together on the mountain [D:146-148].

D:54; D:56; D:146-148

Map of the City and its environsMap obtained by Dotty when she reaches the city where Finnegan is staying. Ignacio traces the routes of Finnegan’s daily walks, and Dotty buys a pistol before setting out to find him [A:281]. The setting is Havana, identified by the lawyer’s letter that brings her there; Ignacio has already told Finnegan that he is not in New Orleans [A:276-277].

A:281; A:276-277

Maps (Angela Cosquin's Father)Maps hand-drawn by Angela Cosquin’s cartographer father on old leather, vellum, and parchment. According to Angela, he first made decorative showpieces, then supplied confidence men with purported treasure maps and old affidavits. Treasure-chest marks such as T, K, and BP suggested Teach, Kidd, and Bartolomo Portuguese [D:259-260]. He also invented shipwreck maps, placing wrecks where he thought ships ought logically to founder among the Antilles’ passages. His master map showed fifty or more real or imaginary wrecks [D:260]. Named ships include Mary Jane, Red Fox, Halcon, Loutre, Jabali, Moonraker, Estrella del Mar, Torre del Marifi, Virgen la mas Benigna, Casa del Oro, Golden Mastiff, Indiaman, Hind, Crane, Blaireau, Megčre, and Renard Volante. Buyers could choose a wreck and even move its location before commissioning supporting papers [D:261].

D:259-260; D:260; D:261

MaravillosaAdmiring Spanish exclamation spoken about Marie Courtois by a man ashore on the Mexican side, paired with “Magnifica” [D:57].

D:57

MarblesSack in Phoebe Anne Ankerson’s suitcase, which Finnegan and Doll have stolen. Its label says the marbles once belonged to Aaron and are intended for Harold Michael; some are agates [D:172].

D:172

MarchMonth of the Brunhilde’s arrival at Naxos, dated March 14, Passion Sunday [D:115]. At Finnegan and Anastasia’s later vigil, the March night is expected to turn chilly, and the moon lacks a week of being full [D:132].

D:115; D:132

March 4thDate in Trinali Peterson’s poem title “To Trinali at Dawn on March 4th.” She says she wrote it on the previous Monday, March 4, and that it symbolizes all March 4ths from the beginning [A:226].

A:226

March 6, 1933Date on which banker Adrian Hilton says the Depression began. He attributes it to the bank moratorium of March 6-9, 1933, in his polemical account of banking and political power [MTM B4:123].

MTM B4:123

Marcus Tullius Cicero (106--43 BC)Uncertain identification. The cited Archipelago passage refers to Cicero as a destination for buying cigars [A:253]; the cited More Than Melchisedech passage names Cicero Brazil among Duffey’s academic acquaintances [MTM B3:99]. Neither passage identifies the Roman orator.

A:253; MTM B3:99

Mare NectarisLunar sea that the Argo is said, in one of its old logs, to have sailed [MTM B13:406].

MTM B13:406

MargieFamiliar form of Margaret Murphey’s name in Loy Larkin’s letter to Finnegan. Loy reports Margie’s love, and Margaret adds “Me too” beneath Loy’s signature [A:27].

A:27

Margie la MagaTheresa Piccone’s name for herself as a magician. She mentions it to Finnegan while explaining that puppetry, concertina playing, and tricks have shaped her fingers [A:108].

A:108

Marianao CoastCoast a few miles from Havana where X says Finnegan and Dotty were killed in a futuristic episode, while refusing to say their deaths were final [MTM B8:238]. Duffey later travels there to investigate Finnegan’s disappearance, guided in part by The Resurrection of Count Finnegan, a painting of his apparent grave and emergence from an ocean cave [MTM B12:367-368].

MTM B8:238; MTM B12:367-368

Marie CelesteJohnny Duckwalk’s mistaken name for the derelict ship when he accuses Le Marin of recycling its story. Le Marin, calling himself a purist, corrects it to Mary Celeste [D:246].

D:246

Marietta (Aunt)One of Henry Salvatore’s two aunts living in his family’s neighborhood, the other being Emily [A:122-123].

A:122-123

Marin, LeCharles Le Marin, one of Finnegan’s companions with Don Barnaby and Johnny Duckwalk in a society described as a dark counterpart to the Dirty Five [A:188] [D:233]. He tells how Castleman’s men infiltrated the Sarcophagus, replacing crewmen with lookalikes at successive ports. His account leaves his own replacement uncertain; he survives the later killing of the loyal crew by hiding and eventually swimming ashore [D:244-246].

A:188; D:233; D:244-246

Marine RoomOrlando bar where Finnegan and Doll Delancy trade jokes about his knowledge, drinking, and supposed lack of brains [D:190].

D:190

Mark (of Cain)Biblical mark associated with Cain in Genesis 4:15. In his transport upon shadowy history, Finnegan asks whether Cain belonged to his people and which people bear the mark, describing a lower facial projection like another nose [D:212-213].

D:212-213

Mark (Salvatore)One of Henry Francis Salvatore’s seven brothers, in the family of Lawrence Salvatore and Mary Genevieve Hebert of Morgan City, Louisiana [A:122].

A:122

Mark McClatchySee McClatchy, Mark.
Market StreetUncertain location. The cited account places Duffey’s newly purchased St. Louis building on Walnut Street, not Market Street [MTM B2:40].

MTM B2:40

Marks (Cabalistic, on fingernails)Witch-signs that Finnegan jokingly says appear on the moons of Theresa Piccone’s fingernails only on Fridays. She replies that she will wear gloves [A:108].

A:108

Marks (Cabalistic, on lead weight)Meaningless cabalistic-looking designs invented by Finnegan and marked on the lead weight he throws through a hotel window during his attack on Seaworthy’s gathering [D:163-164].

D:163-164

Marks (Finishing marks on Sulem's statues)Finishing details Sulem proposes that his uncles add after Hans has roughed out wooden figures with lathes and power saws. The marks would help the machine-made objects seem primitive. Hans refuses the production scheme [A:59].

A:59

Marks (on wrists of Finnegan/Seaworthy)Scar or tattoo inside Seaworthy’s left wrist. He claims to see the same mark beneath Finnegan’s skin, although Finnegan denies having it [D:10]. After the Naxos shooting, X notices an octopus mark on Finnegan’s wrist; Finnegan says it appeared at the shooting and now has that shape [D:156].

D:10; D:156

MarsPlanet to which Hans compares the barren surface of islands passed on the way to Luzon. He jokingly cites people who have visited both places before explaining his account of the birds’ nests harvested there [A:62].

A:62

Marshal of the OperaOfficial who tries to persuade both the Finnegan Image and Margaret Stone to withdraw their demonstrations of humanity at the Decatur Street Opera House. He calls their flames false and their acts pranks; both refuse [MTM B11:348-349].

MTM B11:348-349

MartiniqueOrigin of the chef at Howland Jerome Howland’s Club Royal in Chicago [A:246]. Angela Cosquin also names Martinique among what she calls the seven true passages through the Antilles when describing her father’s shipwreck maps [D:260].

A:246; D:260

Martyr-BellSecond of the summoning bells, brought by Count Finnegan on a raft to a mooring-rock in the shoals north of San Simeon, two days after the Sea-Bell began to sound [MB:575]. It comes from Ste. Genevieve, where the narrative says English raiders killed thirty-nine Christians in 1594. After the raiders’ ship Lord Cramner was wrecked, its salvaged bronze cannon were cast into a bell that rang by itself when enemies of the faith approached [MB:576].

MB:575; MB:576

Marx, Karl (1818--1883)Political writer and, with Friedrich Engels, author of The Communist Manifesto (1848). After reading the New Testament, Stein ranks it alongside Marx and Freud among important books, within his claim that all great books were written by Jews [A:69]. Karl Marx also appears in the place-name Karl Marx Stadt, where the Argo Masters interrupt Ralph Rolfe’s new system of logic [MTM B13:427].

A:69; MTM B13:427

Mary (Old Wooden Ship)Resident of the Old Wooden Ship, listed among its regulars and the women called “salt water widows” [D:216] [D:221]. She works at the clubs and disputes Dutch Duquesne’s boasts about his job and tips, saying that he is a kitchen boy who cleans fish and shucks oysters [D:221].

D:216; D:221

Mary JeanMary Jean, a girl Casey has known since childhood, who marries Hillary Hilton and becomes involved with Casey while he is at college [A:168-169]. Mary Catherine later reports that Mary Jean has married Casey, while considering the union invalid because Mary Jean’s first marriage was in the Church [A:248]. Hillary says he gave Mary Jean the house in their settlement and Casey moved in [A:251-252]. Later More Than Melchisedech passages again call Mary Jean Hilton’s wife and pair the two together [MTM B12:378] [MTM B12:383].

A:168-169; A:248; A:251-252; MTM B12:378; MTM B12:383

Mas de azul?“Bluer?” Ignacio’s Spanish repetition of Finnegan’s remark that the people have become bluer. Finnegan still believes himself in New Orleans, though Ignacio later tells him that he is elsewhere [A:270] [A:276].

A:270; A:276

MassThe Catholic liturgy recurring throughout the cycle. Hans and Marie stop for Mass at St. Marys after talking all night [A:9-10]. Duffey attends at St. Malachy’s in Chicago, where he first sees his future wife [MTM B3:87-88]. Monica reports that Papa Piccone plans accordion music at Vincent and Theresa’s wedding Mass, but Maurine says they are teasing her [A:104-105]. Ramires and Elena Musquiz find Finnegan on their way to Mass in D’Hannis [A:203]. In his later days in Havana, he rises early to attend Mass before his daily walks [A:276-277].

A:9-10; MTM B3:87-88; A:104-105; A:203; A:276-277

Mass of the Holy Precursor MelchisedechMass said over Duffey’s bones aboard the Argo by Biloxi Brannagan in his person of St. Brandon. The narration assigns it to April 31 under the old calendar [MTM B13:443].

MTM B13:443

Mast-Head (Bark/Barque depiction)Finnegan’s drawing of the endangered little boat Henry has dreamed, used as the masthead of The Bark [A:121-122]. In his attack in The Crock, Casey says the barque is wrongly shown as square-rigged rather than composite-rigged and declares it “not Seaworthy” [A:128].

A:121-122; A:128

Mast-Head (Towers school paper)Image of Gregory Hall’s towers on The Towers, the St. Bonaventure school paper dominated by boys from that hall. The rival Chambers uses Audifax O’Hanlon’s drawings of chamber pots with similar silhouettes [A:167].

A:167

Master MapAngela Cosquin’s father’s most elaborate map, showing fifty or more real or imaginary sunken ships. It hangs in his study and attracts confidence men who commission supposed treasure maps from it [D:260]. Named wrecks include Mary Jane, Red Fox, Halcon, Loutre, Jabali, Moonraker, Estrella del Mar, Torre del Marifi, Virgen la mas Benigna, Casa del Oro, Golden Mastiff, Indiaman, Hind, Crane, Blaireau, Megčre, and Renard Volante. Buyers may choose a different location for a wreck as well as supporting papers [D:261].

D:260; D:261

Master of the ShipOffice among the masters of the Argo. Duffey says the man he is to collect at Biloxi has waited thirty years and is himself a Master of the Ship [MTM B13:401]. The man is Biloxi Brannagan, whose wife confirms the long wait [MTM B13:409].

MTM B13:401; MTM B13:409

Masters of the ArgoMembers of the Argo’s interdependent company, including Duffey, Biloxi Brannagan, and Kasmir Gorshok. Each plays a particular role in the others’ lives [MTM B13:446] [MTM B13:454]. An amnestic mechanism normally prevents them remembering the ship while ashore [MTM B12:386]. Absent sailors leave working residues aboard; returning Masters absorb their effigies, which then become part of them [MTM B13:415] [MTM B13:449]. Their recoveries include the Lord’s Table, Sancgreal, Holy Shroud, Ring of the Nebelungs, Philosopher’s Stone, tomb of St. Jude, Northwest Passage, Roland’s Horn, Alaric’s Sword, Aaron’s Rod, Seamless Garment, Baptist’s Head, Magic Flute, Great Mogul Diamond, Iron Crown, and Lost Dutchman Mine. They deliberately lose the perilous Sword and Scabbard of Saint Sécaire three times [MTM B13:422]. They intervene against Ralph Rolfe’s perverse logic, though Casey lets one crucial scrap of writing escape, and they cure a young man of stuttering at Weinsburg [MTM B13:427] [MTM B13:430].

MastodonUncertain entry. The supplied citation does not contain the asserted “Paean to Archipelago” comparison with the mastodont [A:9].

Matthew (Salvatore)One of Henry Francis Salvatore’s nearby uncles, listed among the Salvatore relatives [A:122].

McDearmott, Wimbish A.Name attached to the Panegyrica epigraph at the opening of chapter twelve of The Devil Is Dead. The passage places the sciences of God and man above the science of things and calls John of the Cross an experimental investigator through mysticism [D:176].

McDearmott, Wimbush A.Earlier misspelling. See McDearmott, Wimbish A. [D:176].

McFadden, youngServer at McFadden’s North End Tavern. At Duffey’s request he brings a seventy-two-ounce pitcher of beer and fresh glasses; Duffey also orders onions for himself and Mike Melchiades [MTM B4:141-142].

McGeehan, AuderyMusical friend in Duffey’s Chicago circle, listed with Newbold McGeehan among composers, performers, and stagers whose work ranges from opera to ragtime and string-band music [MTM B3:99].

McGeehan, NewboldOne of Duffey’s musical friends, named with Audery McGeehan in the list of composers, players and stagers. The preceding names are Enniscorthy and Mary Sweeny; Newbold is not a Sweeny [MTM B3:99].

McGonigalFigure appearing at the left hand of the demiurge Teilhard on the altar at St. Michael’s, with McLuhan at the right. All three are transfigured with light while the assembled worshippers call for three tents [GD:497].

McGuigan, FatherPriest who conducts Vincent and Teresa’s wedding in the parish church shared by the Piccones and Stranahans [MTM B5:183]. He joins the men’s discussions of creation and magic [MTM B5:163], rejects their account of human person-making as unlawful metaphor [MTM B5:166], and tries to divert Bagby’s attack on causes the narration says he supports [MTM B5:169]. Monica reports his acceptance of Papa Piccone’s proposed accordion music for the wedding, but Maurine says the story is a joke [A:105]. He permits Theresa to have Masses said for the three children of her other life with Finnegan, though he does not understand her account [A:204].

MTM B5:183; MTM B5:163; MTM B5:166; MTM B5:169; A:105; A:204

McGuire'sHouse whose Philadelphia-made chamber pot, with scrolled porcelain lettering, Duffey can visualize although he has never entered it. The recollection belongs to his appropriation of things noticed in other people’s minds [MTM B1:17].

McIfreann, IanNamed author of Psychologia Nugarum in the epigraph to Chapter Six of The Devil Is Dead. The passage argues that dreams have a topography, with particular dreams recurring among voyagers in particular sea passages, and asks what will happen in the sectors of space [D:80-81].

D:80-81

McMasters, TimothyArtist whose work Duffey sells early in his New Orleans venture and whose ideas contribute to the company’s proposed rebuilding of the world [MTM B6:199].

The pair urge Duffey toward Fleshpot Row, and Josephine joins the hostile response when Demetrio Glauch rejects the company [MTM B4:125] [MTM B4:127]. In “The Casey Machine,” her report in the Underground Eagle declares the machine born from the group’s Particular Judgment, even while recording Casey’s denial that it has been invented [CM:506].

MTM B3:98; MTM B4:125; MTM B4:127; CM:506

McSorley, RolloNewspaperman in Duffey’s Chicago circle, listed with Josephine McSorley [MTM B3:98]. He opposes Tony Apostolo’s opinions [MTM B4:122], encourages Morris Poor’s challenge to Duffey, and bets a hundred dollars against Duffey moving a mule by magic [MTM B4:129]. During the demonstration, Sebastian Hilton strikes and fells both challengers, so they miss the feat. Rollo’s Daily News report, “I was kicked by a flying mule,” ruefully acknowledges the lost bet [MTM B4:131-132]. He later accompanies the group attempting to blackmail Duffey into admitting their ideas to The Crock [MTM B4:140-141].

MTM B3:98; MTM B4:122; MTM B4:129; MTM B4:131-132; MTM B4:140-141

Medina CountyTexas county named, alternatively with Frio County, as the setting of Finnegan’s 105 hours in the chaparral, from Tuesday sundown to Sunday morning. The narrator suggests that he remained northeast of the Frio branch [A:202]. The ancestral city of the buffalo is conjecturally placed across the line in Frio County, with the narrator remarking that no such city is recorded in Medina County [A:205].

Megapolis (in Arcady)Place in Arcady whose surrounding meadows supply the bees’ honey used in Madame Le Mourcheor’s Old Original Juju Joy Pills, according to Don Barnaby’s account [D:249].

Megčre (Ship on Master Map)One of the French treasure ships on the master map used by Angela Cosquin’s father to supply fabricated treasure maps and supporting documents to confidence men. Angela describes all the vessels as treasure-laden and sunk [D:261].
